entities.summary: Erik Gunnar Asplund was a Swedish architect, mostly known as a key representative of Nordic Classicism of the 1920s during the last decade of his life. At this time, he was a major proponent of the modernist style which made its breakthrough in Sweden at the Stockholm International Exhibition (1930). Asplund was professor of architecture at the Royal Institute of Technology from 1931. His appointment was marked by a lecture, later published under the title "Our architectonic concept of space." The Woodland Crematorium at Stockholm South Cemetery (1935-1940) is considered his finest work and one of the masterpieces of modern architecture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key representative of Nordic Classicism and a proponent of modernist architecture, Asplund's work at the Stockholm International Exhibition (1930) influenced Swedish architecture for decades to come. His Woodland Crematorium is considered one of the masterpieces of modern architecture.
